title: Vital Perception
summary: A manifesto poster arguing that design starts beneath the surface, built on an X-ray of my own jaw.
coverAlt: Black poster with an X-ray of a human jaw and the words Vital Perception in red

blocks.heading: The brief
blocks.body: Write a personal design manifesto and express it through one visual metaphor.

blocks.heading: The idea
blocks.body: Most of what makes a design work is invisible, like the structure under skin. An X-ray shows what actually holds a face together. I wanted the poster to say that my job is to see that layer first.

blocks.label: Manifesto drafts. The written manifesto at three stages, from two pages down to the final four lines.

blocks.heading: Process
blocks.body:
The manifesto started as two pages and ended as four lines. I set the type small against the darkest part of the X-ray, so it reads like a note on a medical chart.

The red heartbeat line is the only color, the one sign of life in the image.

blocks.alt: Close-up of the title and the four-line manifesto
blocks.caption: Four lines, set like a note on a chart.

blocks.heading: Reflection
blocks.body: Critique pushed me to cut the title from three words to two. VITAL PERCEPTION is stronger because it doesn’t explain itself.
